# Esther Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 457v–458r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_006_page_001.jpg

---

**6:1** In-that night [ba-laylah ha-hu] the-sleep [shenat] of-the-king fled [nadedah], and-he-said to-bring the-book [sefer] of-the-records [ha-zikhronot], the-words [divrey] of-the-days [ha-yamim]; and-they-were being-read [niqra'im] before [lifney] the-king. **6:2** And-it-was-found written [katuv] that Mordekhai had-reported [higgid] concerning Bigtana and-Teresh, two of-the-eunuchs [sarisim] of-the-king, from-the-guardians [mi-shomrey] of-the-threshold [ha-saf], who had-sought [biqqeshu] to-stretch [lishloach] a-hand [yad] against the-king Achashverosh. **6:3** And-the-king said, "What honor [yeqar] and-greatness [gedullah] has-been-done to-Mordekhai for this?" And-the-servants [na'arey] of-the-king, his-attendants [mesharetav], said, "Nothing [lo-na'asah] has-been-done with-him."

**6:4** And-the-king said, "Who [is] in-the-court [be-chatser]?" And-Haman had-come [ba] to-the-outer [ha-chitsonah] court of-the-house [beyt] of-the-king, to-say to-the-king to-hang [litlot] Mordekhai on the-gallows [ha-ets] which he-had-prepared [hekhin] for-him. **6:5** And-the-servants [na'arey] of-the-king said to-him, "Behold, Haman is-standing [omed] in-the-court." And-the-king said, "Let-him-come-in [yavo]."

**6:6** And-Haman came-in, and-the-king said to-him, "What shall-be-done [mah-la'asot] for-the-man [la-ish] whom the-king delights [chafets] to-honor [bi-yqaro]?" And-Haman said in-his-heart [be-libbo], "To-whom would-the-king delight [yachpots] to-do honor [yeqar] more-than [yoter] to-me?" **6:7** And-Haman said to the-king, "A-man [ish] whom the-king delights to-honor — **6:8** let-them-bring [yavi'u] a-royal [malkhut] garment [levush] which the-king has-worn [lavash], and-a-horse [sus] on-which the-king has-ridden [rakhav], and-on-whose head [rosho] a-crown [keter] of-royalty [malkhut] has-been-placed [nitan]. **6:9** And-let-the-garment and-the-horse be-given [naton] into-the-hand [al-yad] of-a-man from-the-princes [mi-sarey] of-the-king, the-nobles [ha-partemim], and-let-them-clothe [ve-hilbishu] the-man whom the-king delights to-honor, and-let-them-lead-him [ve-hirkivuhu] on-the-horse through-the-street [bi-rechov] of-the-city [ha-ir], and-let-them-proclaim [ve-qare'u] before-him [lefanav], 'Thus [kakhah] shall-be-done to-the-man whom the-king delights to-honor!'"

**6:10** And-the-king said to-Haman, "Hurry [maher], take [qach] the-garment and-the-horse, as you-have-spoken [ki-dibbarta], and-do thus [ken] to-Mordekhai the-Yehudi [ha-Yehudi], the-one-sitting [ha-yoshev] at-the-gate [sha'ar] of-the-king. Do-not-let-fall [al-tappel] a-thing [davar] from-all [mi-kol] that you-have-spoken." **6:11** And-Haman took the-garment and-the-horse, and-he-clothed [va-yalbesh] Mordekhai, and-he-led-him [va-yarkivehu] through-the-street of-the-city, and-he-proclaimed before-him, "Thus shall-be-done to-the-man whom the-king delights to-honor!"

**6:12** And-Mordekhai returned [va-yashov] to the-gate of-the-king. And-Haman hurried [nidchaf] to his-house, mourning [avel] and-with-his-head covered [chafuy rosh]. **6:13** And-Haman recounted [va-yesapper] to-Zeresh his-wife and-to-all his-friends [ohavav] everything [kol] that had-befallen-him [qarahu]. And-his-wise-men [chakhamav] and-Zeresh his-wife said to-him, "If [im] from-the-seed [mi-zera] of-the-Yehudim [ha-Yehudim] [is] Mordekhai, before whom you-have-begun to-fall [linpol], you-will-not prevail [lo-tukhal] against-him, but [ki] you-will-surely-fall [nafol tippol] before-him."

**6:14** While-they-were-yet [odam] speaking [medabberim] with-him, the-eunuchs [sarisim] of-the-king arrived [higgi'u], and-they-hurried [va-yavhilu] to-bring [lehavi] Haman to the-banquet [ha-mishteh] which Ester had-made [asetah].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "the sleep of the king fled":** The Hebrew *nadedah shenat ha-melekh* uses the verb *nadad* (to flee, wander), personifying sleep as something that actively departed. This is not simply "the king could not sleep" but a vivid image of sleep fleeing from him — a pivotal turning point in the narrative.

**v.8 — "keter malkhut" (crown of royalty):** Haman requests that the royal crown be placed on the horse's head, not on the honored man. The Hebrew syntax is ambiguous — *rosho* ("his head") could refer to the horse or the man — but the placement within the sentence about the horse suggests the horse wore the crown-crest, a known Persian custom.

**v.13 — "nafol tippol" (you will surely fall):** The infinitive absolute construction (*nafol tippol*) intensifies the verb, conveying absolute certainty: "you will certainly fall." Haman's own advisors and wife pronounce his doom with the strongest Hebrew verbal construction for inevitability.

*— EMET*
